pr_title: Don't store an HMAC key for longer than we need
pr_body:
The HMAC_CTX structure stores the original key in case the ctx is reused
without changing the key.

However, HMAC_Init_ex() checks its parameters such that the only code path
where the stored key is ever used is in the case where HMAC_Init_ex is
called with a NULL key and an explicit md is provided which is the same as
the md that was provided previously. But in that case we can actually reuse
the pre-digested key that we calculated last time, so we can refactor the
code not to use the stored key at all.

With that refactor done it is no longer necessary to store the key in the
ctx at all. This means that long running ctx's will not keep the key in
memory for any longer than required. Note though that the digested key
*is* still kept in memory for the duration of the life of the ctx.

Fixes #10743

Note: It is debatable whether this should come under the "bug" rules or not, and therefore be eligible for backport to 1.1.1. Since it provides no user visible features, and is a security hardening measure I have flagged it for 1.1.1.
pr_comments: A very nice fix. Thank you!
Pushed to master. The 1.1.1 version apparently needs a slight adjustment. I'll raise a new PR for that.

issue_context.title: HMAC_Init_ex failed to clean up the key buffer, leaving the HMAC key in plaintext
comments:
> Our experiments show that to complete 100million HMAC digests using the same key, init HMAC_CTX with secret key only once will be much faster.

Can you expand a bit more on this statement? How are you performing multiple HMAC operations using the same key if you init the HMAC_CTX only once?

> If you want, I can provide a PR to fix this issue. Thanks.

I actually already have a fix locally. Will raise a PR tomorrow.

A couple of notes about your description of the issue above:

````
  // erase key buffer inside hmac ctx
  memset(m_ctx.key, 0, m_ctx.key_length);
````
This method of cleansing the key is potentially ineffective depending on how clever the compiler is. Some compilers will optimise such memsets away, so it's possible that your 1.0.2 solution isn't doing what you think it is doing.

Additionally, clearing the key may have limited benefits in reality. Although the key itself is cleared the ctx still contains a digested form of the key for the lifetime of the ctx - and this digested form of the key is equally useful to an attacker as the original form (i.e. it could be used to create HMACs as if the attacker had the original key).

Nonetheless, it does seem sensible to avoid storing the original key where we don't have to and therefore I have a fix in #10747.

Noted and thanks!
